title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes 'magasins'. A magasin is a structure M = (M, ≤, ≪, |o|) satisfying axioms Mag 1–Mag 4. The elements are 'cells' or elementary figures. ≤ is the face / sub-figure order, and \tilde X denotes the down-set {X' ≤ X}. ≪ is a finer incidence relation, read as 'X sits in the closure/interior structure of Y'. |o| is a relation of 'external disposition' (disjointness / non-overlap). Figures are down-closed subsets of pairwise compatible elements; compatibility is written here as ≉ and on the next page as ⋔.

On the previous page he defined a 'polyhedral' strengthening of ≪: X ≪_pol Y iff X ≪ Y and, for every face Y' ≤ Y, the sub-figure that X induces on Y' is empty or principal (of the form \tilde X' for one X'). M is prepolyhedral if X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪_pol Y. That page checks that (M, ≤, ≪_pol, |o|) again satisfies Mag 1 (transitivity, using transitivity of induced figures) and Mag 2 (existence of the least Z ≤ Y with X ≪_pol Z).

This page:
- It finishes the verification. Mag 3(a)(b) are trivial because |o| and ≤ are unchanged (the reading 'inv. par dég./déf.' is uncertain), and 'pol-interior-≪' implies interior-≤. Mag 4 involves only ≤ and |o|, so it is untouched.
- Definition: M is polyhedral if X ≪ Y ⇒ X ≪_pol Y, i.e. ≪ = ≪_pol. Then M is automatically prepolyhedral, by taking X ≤ Y.
- For a prepolyhedral M, the associated polyhedral magasin is M^pol = (M, ≤, ≪_pol, |o|). He inserts that it is indeed polyhedral, and M = M^pol iff M is polyhedral.
- Even for polyhedral M one must distinguish two compatibility notions, ≉ and ≉_pol. Definition: X ≉_pol Y iff X ≉ Y and, for all X' ≤ X and Y' ≤ Y, \tilde X' ∩ \tilde Y' is empty or has a greatest element. In other words, any two faces meet in a single common face or not at all: the classical 'intersection property' separating polyhedral (or simplicial-like) complexes from general regular CW complexes.
- Prepolyhedrality is equivalent to X ≉_pol X for all X, hence Y ≉_pol Z for all faces Y, Z ≤ X.
- He introduces Figpol(M) ⊂ Fig(M) (formerly F_M): the figures in which all pairs of elements are pol-compatible.

On the next page he gives the standard example: a circle made of two arcs glued at two vertices lies in Fig but not in Figpol, since the two edges meet in two points with no greatest element. He also states that the algebraic properties of Figpol (sup existence ⇔ union is a figure ⇔ pairwise compatibility) mirror those of Fig.

Purpose: to carve out, inside the axiomatic combinatorial 'analysis situs' (a tame-topology program in the spirit of Esquisse §5), the subclass of polyhedral structures. Here cells meet along faces, as opposed to more general regular-CW-like cell structures.
errors: No substantive mathematical error found. The inserted claim that M^pol is polyhedral holds: the extra condition defining ≪_pol depends only on ≤, which is unchanged, so (≪_pol)_pol = ≪_pol. This presumably explains why he crossed out the explicit formula (M^pol)^pol = M^pol and replaced it by a parenthetical.
Minor gap: the claim that polyhedral implies prepolyhedral 'by taking X ≤ Y' needs the axiom X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪ Y. This is presumably among Mag 1–4 but is not restated here.

The equivalence 'M prepolyhedral ⇔ X ≉_pol X for all X' is only asserted. The two directions mix the induced-figure condition (on ≪_pol) with the intersection condition (on ≉_pol), and they are not obviously identical without unpacking the definition of induced figure.

ideas.what: Polyhedral refinement ≪_pol of the incidence relation: X ≪_pol Y iff each face of Y meets X in a principal sub-figure or not at all; polyhedral magasin = one where ≪ = ≪_pol; reflector M ↦ M^pol
ideas.modern_name: Intersection property for cell complexes / polyhedral vs regular CW face posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (polyhedral complexes); combinatorial form in Björner's CW posets (1984) and the theory of face posets / meet-semilattice conditions
ideas.where_published: Only the general tame-topology program in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5); the magasin axiomatics are unpublished

ideas.what: Pol-compatibility: two cells are pol-compatible if any faces of them meet in empty or a single greatest common face; Figpol(M) ⊂ Fig(M)
ideas.modern_name: Polyhedral (or 'meet-closed') subcomplexes of a cell poset; distinction regular CW complex vs polyhedral complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in combinatorial topology (e.g. Björner, Ziegler)

ideas.what: Axiomatic structure 'magasin' (≤, ≪, |o|) with axioms Mag1–Mag4 as a combinatorial foundation for analysis situs
ideas.modern_name: Closest: axiomatic tame topology / o-minimal-style cell structures; abstract incidence structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Program sketched in Esquisse d'un programme; o-minimality developed by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 mentions 'topologie modérée' only programmatically

missed.claim: This is part of an unpublished axiomatic framework ('magasins', figures, the external-disposition relation |o|) for a combinatorial tame topology. In it, the polyhedral/regular-CW distinction is captured as a reflective refinement M ↦ M^pol of an order-theoretic structure. The framework itself is not in the literature; the specific mathematics on this page is standard.
missed.quote: Le magasin M^pol = (M, ≤, ≪_pol, |o|) est dit le magasin (il est bel et bien polyédral) polyédral associé au magasin prépolyédral M.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents how Grothendieck intended to build tame topology from purely relational axioms. That is of historical interest for comparisons with o-minimality and with combinatorial models of stratified spaces, but it contains no result unknown to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine verifications and definitions inside Grothendieck's unpublished magasin axiomatics. The key notion (faces meet in a single common face, polyhedral vs regular CW) is classical combinatorial topology. Only the framework is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: 'polyidéal' / 'prépolyidéal' throughout should read 'polyédral' / 'prépolyédral', consistent with the next page ('Même si M est polyédral', 'Atelier polyédral').
'(il est bel et bien polyidéal)' should read '(il est bel et bien polyédral)'.
On the previous page 'magma[?]' is surely 'magasin'.
'inv. par dég.[?]' is uncertain; it plausibly means the structure (|o|, ≤) is unchanged ('invariant'/'inchangé') when passing from ≪ to ≪_pol.
In the definition of ≉_pol the condition should read '\tilde X' ∩ \tilde Y' est vide ou a un plus grand élément' (primes on both, as in the image). The next-page transcription drops the primes.
